newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton falls on monsoon prospects.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton falls on monsoon prospects.

text.p: Cotton prices fell on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Progress of the monsoon in the producing centres has brightened the crop prospects which in turn prompted unloading by stockists," one broker said.

Millers kept to the sidelines on expectation of further erosion. In the spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 5 rupees to 1,025/1,070 rupees per maund (37.32 kg). While Punjab saw-ginned fell by 40 rupees to 1,825/1,860 rupees per maund.

In the Gujarat varieties Kalyan cotton dropped 100 rupees to 13,800/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while long-staple Sankar-4 fell by 400/500 rupees to 17,000/17,500 rupees per candy for average variety and at 19,000/20,000 rupees per candy for superior variety.
